title: Foundations: Britpop - The Complete Guide
summary: What Britpop is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Britpop songs: Britpop was 1990s Britain's guitar-pop renaissance: sharp suits, sharper choruses, and a very public rivalry between Oasis and Blur. Melody first, attitude always.

History: Blur's Parklife (1994) and Oasis's Definitely Maybe (1994) and (What's the Story) Morning Glory? (1995) made British guitar pop dominant again; Pulp and Suede added art-school wit.

How the songs work: Britpop favors the keys of G, D, C, A, E. Common forms include Verse–chorus with a big singalong bridge; Music-hall touches: piano, strings. Players should master jangly rickenbacker-style arpeggios first, then lennon-esque nasal vocal delivery. Capo 2 for jangly Britpop chime.
